messages:
Alex Chen: FYI customer ACME-123 reports a sudden p99 spike (~600ms) for API requests. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/ACME-123. Sample x-trace-id: 01abcde-9f. Quick look at the trace shows an unexpected hop through eu-west-1 even though the client is in us-east-1.

support: Auto-created ticket ACME-123 for spike, added priority=P1 and linked traces.

Priya Rao: Can you paste the full trace ID and a sample request-id from logs? Also: did they set region affinity headers or VPC peering?

Alex Chen: Trace id above is 01abcde-9f, sample request-id req_84f3. From Jaeger the spans look like: edge-us-east -> proxy-eu-west -> backend-us-east. Very odd, looks like a mid-flight handoff.

Mateo Silva: Pasted the trace snippet from jaeger (shortened):
```
span: edge-us-east (start)
child: route-proxy (eu-west-1) - 148ms
child: backend-us-east (end)
```
Root span shows routing metadata: route.score=0.82, route.policy=latency_fallback, picked_region=eu-west-1.

Ingrid Novak: @Priya @Mateo possible causes: missing X-Region-Pref header, stale region affinity cache in edge, or fallback policy preferring lower-cost region causing handoff. Any evidence of config change around 2026-03-16T14:00?

Alex Chen: I checked deploy logs — no config deploys around that time. Customer says spike started ~14:01 UTC. They do not set region headers. Reproducer from a us-east host still shows path to eu-west:
```
$ traceroute api.redwood.ai
1 10.0.0.1
2 52.14.123.1 (us-east-1)
3 18.194.12.2 (eu-west-1) 152 ms
4 52.17.122.3
```

Priya Rao: OK can you try forcing header `X-Region-Pref: us-east-1` and see if path stays local? If yes, this is routing/fallback logic. If not, likely an egress or peering issue.

Alex Chen: Did the header test — adding header keeps path in us-east for several requests, latency back to normal. So header overrides the fallback.

Mateo Silva: I'll check infra egress/NAT and peering routes. If edge is preferring eu-west due to capacity scoring, we might have a stale or mis-evaluated capacity hint. Also checking NLB target group health and any cross-region NLB targets.

ops-bot: canary-fallback-alert: model-route vm-23 in eu-west-1 triggered fallback policy at 2026-03-16T14:00:47. Fallback reason: capacity_score_below_threshold.

Ingrid Novak: That matches. If a fallback kicked in for vm-23 in eu-west and policy prefers lower-cost region, some connections may get routed there. But we need to know why the initial decision chose eu-west when client is us-east. Possibly route scoring inversion under load.

Alex Chen: Customer also flagged increased egress billing due to cross-region hops — they want this fixed fast. Marking P1 escalation.

support: Tagging eng-infra and eng-runtime, assigning to Mateo Silva. Adding ACME-123 -> escalation.

Priya Rao: Repro steps posted for eng team:
1) From a us-east host run:
```
curl -H "X-Trace-Id: 01abcde-9f" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
```
2) Observe via `traceroute` or the `x-route-path` response header the hop list.
3) Try with header `X-Region-Pref: us-east-1` to force nearest routing.
```

Mateo Silva: Quick infra update — spotted a NAT gateway in us-east with a transient route leak to our eu transit for ~2m at 14:00 due to a BGP flap with partner peering. I'm rotating NAT and pinning edge affinity caches. Will monitor. :thumbsup:

Ingrid Novak: After rotation, can we adjust fallback policy to prefer region-affinity when trace-origin header absent? Also add an alert when cross-region egress % for a customer goes above 5% compared to baseline.

Alex Chen: Agreed. I'll coordinate with Support to notify ACME about workaround (use X-Region-Pref) and follow up once infra confirms root cause.

support: Noted. Keeping ticket open and will update customer with interim mitigation.

Mateo Silva: Follow-up: NAT route fixed, BGP peer cleared. I'm seeing requests return to us-east routing and p99 back to normal. Will leave monitoring on for 24h and close ACME-123 if stable.

Alex Chen: Thanks all — great triage. If anything else pops up I’ll reopen.
